The other 9 contradicted documented contracts. Five were entry-point rankings: 3 with a correct sibling present, 2 in 5-hop chains. findings.quote: That is part of the finding: unique documented ownership protects.
findings.issue: This is a causal claim the design cannot support. Every held-out instance had unique documented ownership, so no held-out arm lacked it and there is no contrast. The only within-instance manipulations are the two exploratory P4 revisions, n=3 each, and P4-DEPTH changed two docs at once. The blind labels show 9 S1 misses on instances where the documentation already made the gold the unique owner. The held-out ceiling is also confounded with gold salience. Auditors and builders flagged locally odd, self-incriminating golds and ceiling risk: HA-JACKSONCORE's missing '& 0xFF' is a 'well-known Java sign-extension idiom', HC-LANG has 'Salience/ceiling risk... Expect strong models near ceiling', and in HB-COMPRESS the gold's javadoc says 0 to 255 next to an unmasked widening. Mining associates a self-incriminating gold with 0.96 GPT-5.6 Acc@1.
findings.correct_statement: Accuracy was at ceiling on held-out instances built to give the gold unique documented ownership. Several of those golds were also locally salient, and documented ownership was never varied in the confirmatory tier. The study therefore cannot attribute the robustness to documented ownership. That remains a hypothesis supported only by exploratory n=3 revisions.
